retired undocumented /api/auth/register Retired 2026-10-07 (#1376). The legacy credentials signup: it created a User AND a Tenant in one call and recorded no terms acceptance, so it was the second of three self-signup doors and the weaker one. Replaced by the three-step path the wizard uses — POST /api/auth/register/start (unverified user + emailed code, and the only place consent is captured), POST /api/auth/register/verify (proves the address and signs in), POST /api/me/farms (creates the farm). The login page's in-page register form went with it and now links to /start, conditional on social.farm-registration. Its real-DB rollback proof was PORTED, not deleted: tests/integration/tenant-creation-atomicity.test.ts now proves the same property against createTenantWithOwner, which is where the transaction lives on the new path. No client called it — iOS confirmed it calls five auth routes and this is not among them (agri-saas#1371).

retired undocumented /api/t/{tenantSlug}/issues Retired 2026-10-09 (#1479). One of 15 routes under /api/t/{tenantSlug}/issues/** serving a model that does not exist: the GRC teardown removed `Issue`, so the surface operated on `Task` rows through `usecases/issue.ts`, a second write path to the same table. Two measured divergences from the /tasks/** path it duplicated: across 26 write functions it called `bumpEntityCacheVersion` ZERO times (task.ts calls it 17), so a mutation changed the rows and left every reader serving pre-change data for the 60s list-cache TTL; and its 15 `logEvent` calls stamped `entityType: 'Issue'`, so a write to a Task row landed in the hash-chained trail labelled as a nonexistent entity, invisible to any audit query or SIEM filter scoped to Task. Authorization was NOT the divergence — issue.policies.ts was coarser in wording but not weaker in effect. Nothing in the repo called it and agrent-ios confirmed it calls nothing under /issues/. Retired rather than repaired: adding the cache bump and fixing the entityType would have kept a second write path to Task alive for no caller, which is how the two diverged. Deleted with it: usecases/issue.ts, policies/issue.policies.ts, IssueRepository.ts (a deprecated re-export of WorkItemRepository with no src caller), EvidenceBundleRepository.ts, and the ISSUE_CREATED / ISSUE_STATUS_CHANGED automation events, whose only producers were the deleted usecases — leaving those in the catalogue would have let a tenant build a rule that could never fire. tests/unit/issue-guardrails.test.ts now asserts this directory's ABSENCE (it previously early-returned when the directory was missing, which would have been a silent pass on the day of the deletion).

Authorization was NOT the divergence — issue.policies.ts was coarser in wording but not weaker in effect. Nothing in the repo called it and agrent-ios confirmed it calls nothing under /issues/. Retired rather than repaired: adding the cache bump and fixing the entityType would have kept a second write path to Task alive for no caller, which is how the two diverged. Deleted with it: usecases/issue.ts, policies/issue.policies.ts, IssueRepository.ts (a deprecated re-export of WorkItemRepository with no src caller), EvidenceBundleRepository.ts, and the ISSUE_CREATED / ISSUE_STATUS_CHANGED automation events, whose only producers were the deleted usecases — leaving those in the catalogue would have let a tenant build a rule that could never fire. tests/unit/issue-guardrails.test.ts now asserts this directory's ABSENCE (it previously early-returned when the directory was missing, which would have been a silent pass on the day of the deletion).

This path specifically was wired to EvidenceBundleRepository, every method of which was a stub: `create`, `freeze` and `addItem` threw `deprecatedResource`, but `listByIssue` and `listItems` returned `[]` and `getById` returned null. So a GET answered 200 with an empty list — telling an authenticated caller that an issue has no evidence bundles, when the correct answer is that evidence bundles do not exist. No Bundle model appears anywhere in prisma/schema/. The only artefact pinning these three routes in place was tests/integration/evidence-bundle.test.ts, 117 lines of `existsSync` checks asserting the route FILES were on disk — a file-existence check standing in for a behavioural one, which is why nothing flagged the surface in the two months after the models were dropped.
